data.name: Atiksha
data.gender_notes: Atiksha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Atiksha is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘ati’ meaning ‘beyond’ and ‘ksha’ meaning ‘desire’ or ‘longing’. This name is often used to describe a deep, intense yearning for something or someone. In Hindu mythology, Atiksha is a name of Goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, wisdom, and learning. The name Atiksha carries the meaning “Desire, Longing” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Atiksha usually hope their child will grow to embody desire, longing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the deep longing for knowledge, wisdom, and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Atiksha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Desire, Longing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Atiksha total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.
